brand: Hamper'd — hamperd.com — Raleigh residential + commercial laundry
not_this_brand: CYDL (cleanyourdirtylaundry.com) is the sibling campus/student brand. Different palette, logo, characters, pricing, audience and accounts. Nothing from the CYDL campaign may be reused here: not the navy/powder palette, not Archivo Black, not the heart-tag lockup, not the Pile or the Bag characters, not the $100/mo student price, and not the deadpan student voice.
premise: CYDL's campaign sells to people who have no money and no clean socks. Hamper'd sells to people who have money and no time. So the hook is not 'how did they know your room is a mess' — it is the hours. Every post puts a number on the part of the weekend laundry quietly takes, then hands it back. Warmer than CYDL, still plainspoken, family-run rather than clever.

audience.residential: Two-income households, young families, new parents, professionals in Raleigh and surrounding areas. They are not embarrassed about laundry — they are tired of it.
audience.commercial: Short-term rental hosts, salons, barbershops, gyms and studios, small restaurants, clinics. They buy on reliability and turnaround, not on cleverness.

voice_proposal: Warm, direct, receipts-first. Short sentences. Says the real number of hours out loud. No hype, no exclamation marks. NOT the CYDL deadpan — Hamper'd is family-run and should sound like it. CONFIRM BEFORE RENDER.

You did not buy a house to spend Sunday in the basement.

Hamper'd picks it up, washes it, folds it, and brings it back in 24 to 48 hours. One flat monthly rate — {{PRICE}}. No per-pound math, no surprise total at the end.

posts.name: The Thursday Load
posts.sub: You know the smell. You are going to have to run it again.
posts.caption:
The load you started Thursday is still in the washer. You know because you opened it. You are going to have to run it again.

That is the part nobody counts — laundry is not one job, it is a job you have to keep remembering.

We remember it for you. Picked up, washed, folded, back in 24 to 48 hours. {{PRICE}} a month, flat.
hamperd.com
posts.photo_brief: Real photo. Open front-loader with a forgotten damp load inside, shot slightly overhead, cool daylight. Instantly recognisable, mildly funny, not gross.

posts.name: Never Once Empty
posts.sub: It is not a chore. It is a standing appointment you never agreed to.
posts.caption:
Two jobs. Three kids. One hamper that has never once, in its entire life, been empty.

It is not really a chore. It is a standing weekly appointment nobody ever agreed to.

Hamper'd takes the appointment. Flat {{PRICE}} a month, guaranteed weekly pickup slot, back in 24 to 48 hours folded.
hamperd.com
posts.photo_brief: Real photo. An overflowing family hamper on a landing, kids' clothes visible, warm evening light from a hallway. Honest, not staged.

posts.name: What A Sunday Costs

slides.sub: Add it up once. You will not want to add it up twice.
Before a single machine has run.
In front of something you are not really watching.
Let us be honest about this one.
{{PRICE}} a month, flat. Back in 24 to 48 hours, folded.

posts.caption:
Add up one Sunday. Sorting, twenty minutes. Wash and dry, three hours of waiting. Folding, forty-five minutes. Putting it away — tomorrow, probably.

That is most of a day, every week, for as long as you live in that house.

Or: one bag on the porch. {{PRICE}} a month, flat.
hamperd.com
posts.photo_brief: Six real photos, one per slide, same house, same day, same light — a small photo-essay. Sorting on a bed, machine running, folded stack, a full basket by the stairs, then the Hamper'd bag on the porch.
